name: Cardhop
description: Cardhop is a contact manager for Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Vision Pro that uses natural-language input to find, create, edit, organize, and interact with contacts. It combines multiple device contact accounts with lists, relationships, notes, celebrations, business cards, directory search, and communication actions.
agentUseSummary: Cardhop cannot yet be connected to Relay agents because its supported AppleScript, Shortcuts, and URL-handler automation execute through an installed Apple-platform app, while contacts and underlying account credentials remain on the user's device and Relay Marketplace does not currently ship that separate local authority.

blocked.label: Connect Cardhop
blocked.description: Relay does not present a Flexibits Account, subscription, Apple Contacts permission, local contact store, installed-app state, or underlying Google, Microsoft, Exchange, iCloud, or CardDAV account as a Railway Cardhop connection.

blocked.label: Use Cardhop automation
blocked.description: Cardhop's AppleScript parser, Apple Shortcuts actions, and x-cardhop URL handlers require installed-app execution that Relay cannot currently mount or trigger.

blocked.label: Access private contact data
blocked.description: Relay does not inspect Apple Contacts, Cardhop notes, lists, relationships, favorites, recents, local app state, device Keychain credentials, or private contact and directory sessions.

blocked.label: Change contacts or communicate
blocked.description: Creating, editing, moving, listing, exporting, or deleting contacts and initiating calls, messages, emails, meetings, directions, or third-party communication remains unavailable until Relay ships explicit local execution and approval boundaries.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until Relay ships a separately disclosed, user-authorized Apple-device Cardhop connector using supported automation and explicit Contacts permission.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay does not silently bridge OpenClaw to Cardhop's local AppleScript, Shortcuts, URL handlers, contact store, or underlying directory sessions.
Relay does not silently bridge Hermes to Cardhop's local AppleScript, Shortcuts, URL handlers, contact store, or underlying directory sessions.

providerSetup.blocker: Cardhop requires contact accounts to be configured on the Apple device and explicit system Contacts permission. Flexibits says contacts and their account credentials remain on-device, with passwords stored in the device Keychain. Cardhop provides local AppleScript, Apple Shortcuts, and x-cardhop URL automation, including routes that can add a parsed contact immediately, but the reviewed first-party materials do not document a Cardhop server API, OAuth data contract, webhook contract, or remote MCP service. Relay's current Marketplace runtime excludes local-app command execution and cannot truthfully expose this authority from Railway.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request Flexibits, Apple, Google, Microsoft, Exchange, iCloud, CardDAV, or directory credentials; inspect Contacts or Keychain data; run AppleScript or Shortcuts; invoke x-cardhop URLs; automate the app UI; or show Connect. Reconsider after Relay ships a disclosed Apple-device connector with verified app presence, explicit Contacts permission, pinned reviewed tools, per-action approval, result redaction, audit, and no cloud or directory fallback.

evidence.supports: Flexibits describes Cardhop's natural-language contact management, group communication, Shortcuts support, multiple device contact accounts, and on-device contact storage.
Cardhop requires contact accounts to be added to macOS and explicit system permission to read the user's contacts.
Flexibits states that Cardhop contacts and contact-account credentials remain on-device, passwords stay in the device Keychain, and Flexibits does not receive those credentials.
Cardhop documents Mac-local AppleScript and x-cardhop URL parsing, including an AppleScript option to add a parsed contact immediately without confirmation.
Cardhop documents local URL handlers for parsing contact actions, adding contacts, showing contacts or views, and opening app preferences.
Cardhop release notes document Shortcuts actions for finding contacts, opening search, performing contact actions, creating or changing contacts, adding notes, and reading upcoming celebrations.
